lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the AutoRound low-bit surface has been consolidated, regressed, and re-landed upstream within eleven months, and the last re-landing happened the day after this fork's pin. (1) AutoRound in vLLM history: support arrived as a dedicated auto_round.py quant config in #17850 (merged 2025-05-20, accepting bits 2/3/4/8); #31688 '[Quantization] Deprecate Long Tail of Schemes' (Robert Shaw, merged 2026-01-08, first release v0.14.0, tag 2026-01-16) introduced DEPRECATED_QUANTIZATION_METHODS = [deepspeedfp, tpu_int8, ptpc_fp8, fbgemm_fp8, fp_quant, bitblas, gptq_marlin_24, gptq_bitblas, hqq, experts_int8, ipex, auto-round, rtn, petit_nvfp4] with a hard raise unless --allow-deprecated-quantization - note v0.14.0 gated rather than removed them; per-scheme code deletions followed (BitBlas #32683 2026-01-28, petit NVFP4 #32694 2026-04-04; at the fork pin the deprecated list is down to fbgemm_fp8/fp_quant). #31716 'Consolidate Intel Quantization Toolkit Integration in vLLM' (Yi Liu, merged 2026-01-14, first release v0.15.0) deleted auto_round.py (454 lines) and moved everything into the INC quant method: INCConfig.override_quantization_method maps HF quant_method 'auto-round' to 'inc', so 'auto-round' checkpoints still load even though the CLI name is deprecated. The current docs (docs/features/quantization/inc.md at the pin) state 'On Intel platforms... Currently, vLLM supports: W4A16, W8A16' and link the OPEA 2-3-bits HF collection. (2) The outline's '#39778 = AutoRound W4A16 first-class' claim needs correction: #39778 '[Quantization][Autoround][Toolkit] Add W4A16 Support' (Zhenzhong Xu, Intel; merged 2026-05-14, first release v0.21.1rc0) is the XPU/CPU path - it adds the ARK backend (INCARKLinearMethod via auto_round_lib>=0.13.0 in requirements/xpu.txt) and refactors the XPU oneDNN W4A16 method; it touches no CUDA code. On CUDA, W4A16 arrived earlier through #31716's consolidation into INC and routes to Marlin. (3) The CUDA gating at the fork pin (79378fe6e8, 2026-08-27), verified in-tree: vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/inc/schemes/inc_wna16_linear.py _build_gptq_method accepts only (bits=4, sym) and (bits=8, sym) via gptq_type_map {4: uint4b8, 8: uint8b128} and raises NotImplementedError for anything else ('Only 4-bit and 8-bit symmetric quantization is supported with Marlin kernels'); the AWQ route accepts bits 4/8 with zero_point=not sym (AutoAWQMarlinLinearMethod, Marlin uint4+zp is sm75-capable). So at the pin, GPTQ-format AutoRound W2/W3 and asymmetric-GPTQ W4 do not load on CUDA at all. This is a 2026-05 regression, not a long-standing gap: #38288 '[Quant] Consolidate GPTQ: rename gptq_marlin.py to auto_gptq.py' (merged 2026-05-15, first release v0.22.0-era) deleted gptq.py (399 lines, the exllama gptq_gemm path) which since #26092 (2025-10-24, GPTQv2 format) had accepted bits 2/3/4/8 incl. asymmetric via exllama. (4) The Humming lane: inclusionAI/humming is a JIT-compiled GEMM kernel library for quantized inference supporting 'any weight type under 8-bit' - symmetric INT1-8 and INT1-8 with dynamic zero point - with FP16 activations on SM75+ (Turing floor; BF16 needs SM80+), dense and MoE GEMM, packaged at ~100KB requiring only PyTorch+NVCC. vLLM integration: #34556 '[Quantization] add humming quantization kernel' (jinzhen-lin, merged 2026-04-24 - the same author as the sm75 Marlin port #29901), then #46389 'Humming support for 2/3/5/6/7-bit pack-quantized weight-only inference' (HDCharles, merged 2026-06-24, first release v0.25.0); humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.12 is a standard requirement in requirements/cuda.txt. The compressed-tensors RFC #719 (HDCharles, opened 2026-06-01) records the design: WINT[B]A16 first priority, packing settled on 'padded 32-bit chunks' with ~6.25-12.5 percent storage overhead for the non-divisor widths (3/5/6/7), and the admission that humming's CT-format repack 'only works for 2/4/8 bits currently since those don't have padding'. (5) The decisive event: PR #52890 'add 2/3/5/6/7 CUDA support in AutoRound format' (wenhuach21, created 2026-08-19, MERGED 2026-09-07 - eleven days after the fork pin) extends INCConfig.SUPPORTED_BITS to {2..8} and routes CUDA bits {2,3,5,6,7} (both auto_gptq and auto_awq packing, linear and MoE) to humming via _build_humming_linear_method/_build_humming_moe_method while 4/8 stay on Marlin; the PR's own test model is Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound, and its comment says this 'mirrors compressed-tensors WNA16, whose 5/6/7-bit biased scalar types also fall back to humming at kernel selection'. Until a release carries it, that checkpoint's model card instructs users to pip install from the PR branch (refs/pull/52729/head, the closed predecessor #52729 'Restore CUDA support for 2-bit and 3-bit AutoRound formats'). (6) compressed-tensors itself: the repo moved from the neuralmagic org to vllm-project around 2025-10 (link-update PR #495 by mgoin merged 2025-10-16), following Red Hat's acquisition of Neural Magic (announced 2024-11, closed 2025-01); the fork venv carries compressed-tensors 0.17.0 (2026-06-03) whose METADATA already says Home-page github.com/vllm-project/compressed-tensors, Author 'The vLLM Project'; latest release v0.18.0 (2026-08-08). The #458 bug object: issue #458 'Support zero-point decompression for asymmetric quantization (packed compressor)' (Etelis, opened 2025-09-09, closed) - 'zero-points are packed during compression but were not unpacked during decompression', which 'prevented loading and inference for models using GROUP or CHANNEL strategies' on the transformers/AutoModel decompression path; it tracks llm-compressor #1704 (dsikka, 2025-08-05, test model nm-testing/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0-w4a16-asym-awq-e2e) and was fixed by PR #463 (Etelis, merged 2025-10-30; follow-up to the accidentally history-rewritten #459), first shipped in compressed-tensors v0.13.0 (2025-12-16) - the fix (unpack_from_int32 on weight_zero_point in PackedQuantizationCompressor.decompress when not symmetric and strategy in PACK_ZP_STRATS) is present in the fork's 0.17.0. The error string 'Decompression of packed zero points is currently not supported' surfaced publicly in llm-compressor #2099 (2025-12-05, an asymmetric AWQ Cohere model). Important scoping: #458/#463 fixed only the decompress-to-float path; the serving path still rejects asymmetric W2/W3 - in vLLM, CompressedTensorsWNA16's WNA16_ZP_SUPPORTED_TYPES_MAP = {4: uint4, 8: uint8} raises for asymmetric num_bits outside {4,8} at scheme construction, before any kernel is consulted. (7) AutoRound upstream (intel/auto-round, 1606 stars, pushed 2026-09-07) released v0.13.0 (2026-05-31), v0.14.x (July 2026), v0.15.0 (2026-08-31); the AutoScheme mixed-bit recipe generator ('2.8 bpw' models) arrived with >0.14.2. (8) Checkpoint landscape on HF (queried 2026-09-07): the Intel org carries 102 AutoRound models; the operator's Qwen3-class ~27B target is directly covered - Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound (46,269 downloads, updated 2026-05-21, autoround 0.13.0: bits=4 sym=true group_size=128 packing auto_round:auto_gptq, 97 MTP layers left at bits=16 in extra_config, dtype bfloat16), Intel/Qwen3.5-27B-int4-AutoRound, Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound (1,818 downloads, updated 2026-08-24, autoround 0.15.0: global bits=2 sym=true group_size=64 auto_gptq packing with 245 layers at 3-bit and 97 at 16 in extra_config, dtype bfloat16 - the concrete operator-class W2/W3 mixed checkpoint, explicitly 'requires vLLM PR #52890' and noting 'the 2-bit and 3-bit kernels are currently not as efficient as the 4-bit and 8-bit kernels'), and Intel/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int2-mixed-CT-AutoRound (582 downloads, 2026-08-14: compressed-tensors pack-quantized, quantization_status=compressed, group_0 = 4-bit sym g128 on attention+shared-experts, group_1 = 2-bit sym g64 on the MoE experts - a single checkpoint exercising both the Marlin and humming routes). The OPEA '2-3 bits' collection holds six symmetric INC-baked models: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-int2-sym-inc (group_size 32) and -int3-, Qwen2-VL-72B-Instruct-int2, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct-int2, DeepSeek-R1-int2-mixed-sym-inc, DeepSeek-R1-int2-gptq-sym-inc (quant_method gptq, bits=2, g64; autoround 0.4.2/0.4.5 era). Community W2/W3 variants exist per model (YCWTG/Qwen3-Coder-Next-int2-mixed-AutoRound; HaberstrohSystems/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-int2-mixed-AutoRound-24GB-SGLang, a 24 GB single-card SGLang-oriented build).
lacuna.sm75_viability: What actually runs on Turing today, per format. (1) W4A16 symmetric GPTQ-format (the Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound class): fully servable on sm75 by upstream releases since v0.14.0 - the 'auto-round' quant_method is overridden to INC, INCWna16LinearScheme routes (4, sym) to AutoGPTQLinearMethod, GPTQ Marlin get_min_capability is 75 (lowered in #29901/#31000, Dec 2025), groups -1/32/64/128 with thread-tile padding (#45295/#45703). On this host the incumbent measures 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 and 0.60 at M1 (plan/0002 records). (2) W4A16 asymmetric + ZP: two upstream layouts diverge - AWQ packing (AutoRound format=auto_awq, zp in the scale domain) routes to AutoAWQMarlinLinearMethod with zero_point=True and Marlin's has_zp path accepts scalar uint4 on cc>=7.5, so AWQ-packed asym W4 is sm75-servable upstream; GPTQ packing with packed zero points is rejected (INC raises for sym=false). For this fork neither gate matters: the staged strategy is zero-point-capable by construction (the plan/0002 reference contract), so the adapter maps AutoRound signed-int4 + zp into the staged layout directly - the README calls this 'the shortest path to serving AutoRound W4 on Turing', and nothing found upstream contradicts it. (3) W2A16 (16 weights per u32, pack_factor exactly 16, no padding): at the fork pin there is NO upstream path on any CUDA GPU (INC raises NotImplementedError; CT sym-2-bit reaches humming only if one goes through the compressed-tensors format, which #46389/v0.25.0 made sm75-legal since HummingLinearKernel.get_min_capability()=75); post-#52890 (merged 2026-09-07, un-released at research time) the GPTQ/AWQ-packed AutoRound W2 routes to humming, whose README floor is 'all NVIDIA GPUs from SM75+ (Turing) and beyond' with FP16 activations and symmetric INT1-8 or INT1-8 dynamic-zero-point. No humming-on-Turing throughput numbers are published anywhere I could find - the PR test on Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8 was run by Intel authors, almost certainly on data-center silicon, so humming's sm75 speed is an open measurement. (4) W3A16: the padded case - Fraction(32,3) packing, ceil-padded chunks (10 values per 32-bit word, 2 pad bits, ~6.25 percent storage overhead), the exact case RFC #719 flags ('padded 32-bit chunks') and the one where humming's own CT repack was originally limited to the divisor widths; both #46389 and #52890 parametrize bits=3 in their tests, so the padded path is wired. Same sm75 story as W2. (5) The MoE case matters for the operator: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int2-mixed-CT mixes 4-bit sym g128 (attention/shared experts -> Marlin, sm75 fine) with 2-bit sym g64 experts (-> humming dense/MoE GEMM); #52890 added _build_humming_moe_method for exactly this shape. (6) Hard blockers that remain, all previously characterized on this host: no BF16 (both target checkpoints ship dtype=bfloat16, so the plan/0005 stage-10 bf16->fp16 recast with overflow check is a prerequisite for serving them on sm75 regardless of quant format); the engine row (plan/0005 stage 11 - the fork's retained Turing engine, Triton attention as portable fallback) gates any end-to-end serving claim, not the GEMM rows themselves; Marlin's group-size set {-1,32,64,128} covers all surveyed checkpoints (g128/g64/g32). Fallback semantics to keep loud: since #46389/#52890, low-bit layers silently route to HummingLinearKernel (an INFO log 'Using HummingLinearKernel for CompressedTensorsWNA16' at best); humming JIT-compiles at first use (NVCC required; humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.12 matches this host's CUDA 13.3 build) adding one-time load latency; if the humming package is absent the kernel chooser falls through to ValueError 'Failed to find a kernel that can implement the WNA16 linear layer'. The attention-backend candidate matrix does not gate this item beyond the standing engine row. For determinism of viability claims: W4-sym sm75 loading is upstream-documented and host-verified; W2/W3 sm75 loading is upstream-code-verified (capability constants and kernel tables) but not yet host-run - the one-session probe below settles it.
lacuna.upstream_base: Dated ledger for the AutoRound low-bit surface, keyed to what the fork can rebase onto. 2024-04/07: GPTQ Marlin (#3922) and AWQ Marlin (#6612) land, sm80+ only. 2025-05-20: vLLM #17850 adds AutoRound as auto_round.py (bits 2/3/4/8 accepted at config level; CUDA execution via GPTQ/AWQ Marlin and exllama). 2025-08-05: llm-compressor #1704 (dsikka) requests zero-point decompression for the packed compressor. 2025-09-09: compressed-tensors #458 (Etelis) files the concrete bug - asymmetric packed zero points not unpacked on load (GROUP/CHANNEL strategies fail to load/infer on the decompression path). 2025-10-16: compressed-tensors org move neuralmagic -> vllm-project (PR #495, mgoin; post Red Hat/Neural Magic consolidation). 2025-10-24: vLLM #26092 adds GPTQv2 low-bit/asymmetric via the exllama gptq_gemm kernel - W2/W3 GPTQ loadable on CUDA (exllama min capability 60, so sm75 included). 2025-10-30: compressed-tensors #463 (Etelis) merges the zero-point decompression fix; ships in v0.13.0 (2025-12-16). 2025-12-16/19: vLLM #29901 + #31000/#31008 bring Marlin to sm75 (W4A16 sym GPTQ/AWQ + W8A16 reach Turing). 2026-01-08: vLLM #31688 deprecation gate for the long tail incl. 'auto-round' (first release v0.14.0, tag 2026-01-16); per-scheme removals follow through spring 2026. 2026-01-14: vLLM #31716 deletes auto_round.py, consolidates into INC with the auto-round -> inc override (first release v0.15.0); inc.md from here on states 'Currently, vLLM supports: W4A16, W8A16' for Intel platforms. 2026-04-24: vLLM #34556 (jinzhen-lin) adds the humming quantization kernel. 2026-05-14: vLLM #39778 '[Quantization][Autoround][Toolkit] Add W4A16 Support' merges - XPU/CPU ARK backend via auto_round_lib>=0.13.0 (first release v0.21.1rc0). 2026-05-15: vLLM #38288 deletes gptq.py (exllama gptq_gemm) - CUDA 2/3-bit GPTQ and GPTQv2 asymmetric drop out of main (first release v0.22.0-era). 2026-06-01: compressed-tensors RFC #719 (HDCharles) - humming for CT WNA16, padded-32-bit-chunk packing decision. 2026-06-04: vLLM #44340 CT WNA8O8Int + WNInt embeddings (mgoin). 2026-06-24: vLLM #46389 'Humming support for 2/3/5/6/7-bit pack-quantized weight-only inference' (HDCharles; first release v0.25.0) - symmetric CT pack-quantized W2/W3/W5/6/7 become sm75-legal via humming. 2026-08-31: auto-round v0.15.0 (AutoScheme mixed-bit recipes; the bpw2.8 checkpoints). 2026-08-19: vLLM #52729 opened ('Restore CUDA support for 2-bit and 3-bit AutoRound formats'), closed in favor of #52890. 2026-09-07: vLLM #52890 'add 2/3/5/6/7 CUDA support in AutoRound format' (wenhuach21) MERGED - INC SUPPORTED_BITS {2..8}, CUDA bits {2,3,5,6,7} -> humming (linear + MoE), 4/8 stay Marlin; first release will be the next v0.29-era train (no release contains it as of 2026-09-07). Consequence for the fork: the pin 79378fe6e8 (2026-08-27) is the last-good base that predates #52890; rebase choice is absorb #52890 (getting the humming INC routing for free as the comparison incumbent) or implement the fork's own W2/W3 strategy rows against the pin and race the release train. compressed-tensors last-good: 0.17.0 in the fork venv (fix #463 present since 0.13.0); latest upstream 0.18.0 (2026-08-08).

effort_value.effort_estimate: An adapter + registry-rows increment on the existing plan/0003-0004 machinery, not a new campaign. Work items in dependency-friendly order: (1) W4A16-asym adapter - map AutoRound's signed-int4 + group-scales + packed-zp GPTQ layout into the staged strategy (zero-point already in the reference contract; the unpack semantics are fully specified by compressed-tensors pack_to_int32/unpack_from_int32 and AutoRound's documented qweight [in/pack, out] sequential order) - roughly one to two sessions including the oracle case set; (2) W2A16 strategy row - 16-weights-per-u32 extraction, a wider-grain sibling of the landed nibble machinery, cheapest dequant of all (2-bit extract + group scale), one row through the standing gates - one to two sessions; (3) W3A16 row - the padded 3-bit packing (10 values per u32 + 2 mask bits), same gates plus pad-bit-contamination oracle cases - one to two sessions; (4) format-axis wiring (stage 5) for the three rows plus the incoming-format checklist rows - one session; (5) optional comparison incumbent - cherry-pick #52890 or install the PR-branch wheel on the sm75 host to benchmark humming on TU102 - half a session. Total: roughly one to two weeks of sessions; everything rides the landed float64-oracle + ladder + dispatch-table machinery, so no new harness.
effort_value.unlocks: Serves the operator's exact target-class checkpoints that upstream releases cannot serve today: Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound (W2/W3 mixed, ~7-10 GB of weights - the plan/0005 'W2A16 ~7 GB -> single-card' case, currently requiring an unmerged-PR vLLM build), Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound (W4A16, single-card), and Intel/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int2-mixed-CT-AutoRound (MoE with 2-bit experts, exercising the MoE grouped forward from plan/0002). Fills the low end of the format ladder so the operator's 27B-class serving targets on 2x RTX 6000 have a footprint option between W4 (~14 GB) and FP8 (~14 GB emulated) down to W2 (~7 GB); makes the fork the only release-quality sm75 runtime for the OPEA 2-3-bit collection (Llama-3.3-70B int2/int3, Qwen2.5-72B int2, DeepSeek-R1 int2) once the engine row holds; and completes three concrete rows of the stage-5 format axis, proving the 'new format = adapter + row' contract with the hardest cases (non-divisor bit width, packed zp).
effort_value.dependency_order: Repo-internal prerequisites already landed: reference backend + float64 oracle with zero-point cases (plan/0002), kernel ladder + propose.py row interface + winner gates (plan/0003/0004), the staged/regdeq kernel family (W4 nibble machinery that W2 widens and W3 pads), MoE grouped forward (oracle-validated, needed for the int2-mixed MoE checkpoint), dispatch-table selection. Must land first: the stage-1 checkpoint adapter IR extension for GPTQ/AWQ/CT pack layouts (weights, scales, zp triples) - it is the shared substrate for all three rows - and the stage-10 bf16->fp16 recast, since both target checkpoints ship dtype=bfloat16 and nothing runs on sm75 without it. Then: W4-asym adapter (immediately, shortest path, zero new kernel work), W2 row (parallel - independent extraction width), W3 row (after W2; shares the padded-chunk handling), format-axis selection wiring (stage 5) once at least one row is oracle-clean. The humming comparison (cherry-pick #52890 or PR-branch wheel) is independent and can proceed in parallel from day one. External prerequisites: none - the packing formats are documented in open code (compressed-tensors compressors/pack_quantized/helpers.py), the checkpoints are public on HF, and humming-kernels is pip-installable.
effort_value.risk_notes: Numerics: (1) zero-point semantics differ by layout - GPTQ-format stores integer zp packed alongside weights (must be unpacked and applied in the accumulator domain), AWQ-format folds zp into the scale domain as a subtraction on dequantized values, and compressed-tensors' unpack_from_int32 re-signs by subtracting 2^(bits-1); the adapter must not conflate them, and the oracle needs one case per layout; (2) the 16x relative-scaling nibble-pair finding (MEMORY 2026-08-28: the m16n8k8 B fragment packs k,k+1 into one byte) applies directly to the W4 nibble path and generalizes to W2's 2-bit planes - the staging-side interleave must be width-aware or the oracle passes false-clean on symmetric test weights; (3) W3 padding: pad bits outside the 10-values-per-word window must be masked before extract; a wrong mask is silent (contributes garbage weights) unless an oracle case uses non-zero pad bits - the compressed-tensors packer pads with zeros, so the fork's repacker must too and must assert it; (4) asymmetric oracle coverage: a symmetric-only case set would miss a zp-index transpose - the plan/0002 seven-case suite already includes zero-point cases and must be kept. Silent fallbacks: upstream now routes low-bit to humming with only an INFO log; the fork's dispatch must mark kernel selection loudly per row (the standing discipline); humming JIT-compiles at first use so a cold-load latency spike is expected and must not be mistaken for kernel slowness in benchmarks (warm before timing, per the locked-clock protocol). Upstream drift: HIGH and immediate - #52890 merged 2026-09-07, one day after the pin; the fork's W2/W3 rows now race an upstream incumbent (humming) rather than a vacuum, and the next release (v0.29-era) will make 'vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound' work out of the box on sm75-capability hardware - the fork's differentiator must be measured sm75 speed or attested numerics, not mere loadability. MoE: the int2-mixed checkpoint needs the W2 row wired into the MoE grouped forward, and expert-count x group-64 layouts stress the repack paths differently from dense. Benchmark validity: Intel's #52890 pass on the bpw2.8 model reports 'pass' with no public accuracy or throughput artifacts - treat as existence proof only. Checkpoint dtype: both 27B targets are bfloat16; numerics claims on sm75 require the recast path and its overflow check, mixing two recast domains (weights bf16->fp16 exact; scales are small floats, safe).
effort_value.determinism_class: All three rows are deterministic integer-extraction + fixed-order GEMM loops: the dequant is a pure function of the packed word, group scale, and zp (exact in the float64 oracle; fp16 error enters only at the multiply-accumulate), tile traversal is fixed, and the non-split paths have no atomics - bitwise per configuration, so the 2x-oracle-pass and median-of-N discipline carries over unchanged. The upstream comparison incumbent differs by class: GPTQ Marlin offers a locks-based fixed-order global reduction (bitwise; caller-zeroed workspace) alongside an atomic variant (statistical; run-to-run fp rounding varies with slice arrival order) - the winner-gate transcript must record which epilogue a benchmarked config used; humming allocates a 1024-int32 lock array for its global reduction (same locks family as Marlin - fixed-order under barrier acquire in the deterministic mode, but the JIT-compiled kernel's reduction order is not documented and must be classed empirically before any bitwise claim about it). Run-to-run variance sources here: none in the fork rows beyond clock/thermal (methodology handles), plus humming's JIT compile cache state (first-call vs cached - timing methodology must separate compile from execute). Restart-to-restart: workspace/lock zero state (the standing caller-contract and CUDA-graph WS-zero ordering note from turing_lab/probes/cuda_graph_validation.md applies to any locks-based epilogue the fork adopts from the Marlin family). What the float64-oracle gate needs to hold: asymmetric-weight cases per layout (GPTQ packed zp, AWQ scale-domain zp, CT re-signed zp), group-boundary cases at g32/g64/g128, W3 padded-chunk cases with asserted-zero pad bits, and the K-deep accumulation case (K=11008-class) for any fp16-accumulator variant; median-of-N timing only after oracles pass, per the standing rules.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: the operator's target-class W2/W3 checkpoint now exists and is public (Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound, published 2026-08-24, ~2.8 bpw, single-card footprint) and no released vLLM can serve it - the model card itself instructs users to install an unmerged PR branch, so on the fork's pinned release even ignoring sm75 it does not load, meaning the fork's adapter is not redundant with its own base; W4A16-asym through the staged strategy is nearly free work (the reference contract is already zero-point-capable, so it is an adapter, not a kernel); W2A16 decode is bandwidth-bound - the fork's proven strongest regime (dispatch-table wins at M<=8), and the cheapest dequant of all formats; three concrete rows complete the stage-5 format axis with the hardest cases, hardening the 'adapter + row' contract before MXFP4/NVFP4 arrive. Against: upstream #52890 merged 2026-09-07 - the 'no sm75 kernel path exists' window closed the day after the fork pin, and the next release train (v0.29-era) will serve these checkpoints on Turing via humming with zero fork effort, so the loadability argument expires on the order of weeks; humming claims SM75+ with arbitrary sub-8-bit widths and MoE GEMM, so the fork must win on measured sm75 speed or attested numerics rather than capability; and humming-on-Turing throughput is unpublished, meaning the race outcome is genuinely unknown until the probe runs. Window-closing risk: HIGH for the capability claim (closes with the next vLLM release), LOW for the speed claim (JIT kernels tuned on newer silicon are frequently mediocre on old silicon; the fork's sm75-specialized staged family has beaten generic paths before). Net: do the W4-asym adapter immediately (pure upside), run the humming-on-TU102 probe before spending kernel-ladder budget on W2/W3 rows, and gate the W2/W3 row investment on that probe's result.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, one session, three steps. (1) Adapter-oracle step (no GPU): pull the shard headers of Intel/Qwen3.6-27B-int4-AutoRound and Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound, implement the unpack reference on CPU directly from compressed-tensors pack_to_int32 semantics (GPTQ qweight [in/pack, out], sequential little-endian order value >> (bits*i); W2 = 16 values/u32; W3 = 10 values + 2 pad bits), and assert exact equality with a float64 dequant of a few real tensors including zp application - this proves the layout reading before any kernel work. (2) Fork-row step: wire the W4-asym adapter into the staged strategy and run the standing 2x float64 oracle with the asymmetric-weight, group-boundary (g32/g64/g128), and W3-pad cases added - all-tensor oracle on the real checkpoint's first layers, timing forbidden until clean. (3) Incumbent step (the decisive one): on the locked-clock TU102 host, pip install vLLM from the #52890 PR branch (or cherry-pick the three-file diff onto the pin) with humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.12, load Intel/Qwen3.8-27B-bpw2.8-AutoRound with dtype=float16 and a small max-model-len, confirm humming JIT-compiles and generates on sm75 at all (existence + cold-compile time), then marlin_bench-style the humming W2/W3 GEMM at the 27B shapes across M in {1,8,32,512} under the standing protocol. Decision rule: if humming does not run on sm75 or lands far below the fork's staged-family efficiency, the W2/W3 rows proceed with the incumbent beaten a priori; if humming is competitive, the W2/W3 rows shrink to the adapter + format-axis entry with humming as incumbent delegation (the stage-5 'incumbent delegation unchanged when no adapter matches' clause inverted: adapter matches, incumbent wins) and the kernel budget moves to the plan/0002 acceptance lane instead.
